# Linked Data Publishing

Publishing linked data means shipping a web page that is simultaneously readable by a person and
parseable as a graph by a machine, with every entity identified by an IRI that can actually be
fetched. Three obligations follow, and `Information-Systems-Modelling` lab 6 meets all three.

## 1. The same facts in two syntaxes, from one source

Every page carries **RDFa 1.1** attributes inline in the body markup *and* a **JSON-LD** block in the
head. Both are emitted by one renderer from the JSON files in `lab6/app/data/` — `builds.json`,
`communities.json`, `marketplace.json`, `testruns.json`, `users.json`, `site.json`. The data is the
ABox; the vocabulary comes from `lab6/vocabulary/ontology.ttl` and `mc-context.jsonld`.

This is the whole point of the lab and the subject of [[generate-markup-instead-of-hand-writing-it]]:
the previous version hand-wrote both syntaxes into six HTML files, so each fact existed in two to
four places and could drift.

## 2. Dereferenceable IRIs — 303 plus content negotiation

An IRI that names a *thing* (a build) must not be confused with the IRI of a *document about* that
thing. `lab6/app/src/server.js` implements the W3C recommendation directly:

- request `/resource/build-falcon` with `Accept: text/html` → **303 See Other** to the human page
- request it with `Accept: application/ld+json` → the data graph

> "every resource IRI is dereferenceable with content negotiation (W3C Linked Data best practice):
> a browser (Accept: text/html) is redirected to the human page, while an RDF client
> (Accept: application/ld+json) gets the data graph at the same /resource/<id> URL."
> — Information-Systems-Modelling/lab6/app/src/server.js, 2026-07-09

The server is `node:http` and nothing else — see [[zero-dependency-no-build-step]]. The same source
tree runs as a live SSR server (`npm run dev`) or emits a static site into `dist/`.

## 3. A shared vocabulary first, a private one only where needed

Terms come from **schema.org** wherever schema.org has them, and from the `mc:` namespace of the
lab 5 TBox where it does not — see [[schema-org-first-custom-vocab-fallback]] and
[[ontology-modelling-tbox-abox]]. `src/rdf/vocabmap.js` applies the rule programmatically rather
than by hand, and writes a `VOCAB MAP` provenance comment into every generated page by walking that
page's own graph, so the comment cannot go stale the way a hand-maintained one would. That is
[[provenance-and-limits-stated-inline]] applied to machine-readable output.

## Verification is a script that prints, not a test that fails

`lab6/app/scripts/validate.py` uses `rdflib` to count triples per page and site-wide. The README
reports 333 triples across the site and 76 for `build-falcon.html`.
